## Code Review Report

### Review Summary

This PR replaces the wiki maintainer's streamed prompt flow with a direct call into `wiki_extract` and adds unit coverage for the new path. The main regression is that the new implementation drops the configured provider, host, and model parameters, so wiki extraction no longer honors the `eval_model` transport settings that the rest of the pipeline uses. Documentation and tests were updated incompletely and currently describe or enforce the old/new behavior inconsistently.

**Files Reviewed:** 8
**Findings:** 1 Critical, 2 Warning, 0 Suggestion

### Findings

#### Critical Findings

[C-01] Wiki maintainer drops provider, host, and model parameters when calling the extractor
Category: Correctness
Severity: Critical
File: src/presentation/agents/wiki_maintainer.py
Lines: 59-64
Description: The previous implementation passed the full `ModelConfig` into `provider.stream_text(...)`, so `eval_model` settings such as provider selection, custom host, and query parameters were honored. The new code now calls `update_wiki_from_chapter(..., model=model_config.name)` on a worker thread, which strips everything except the bare model name before the request reaches the tool layer. In `src/tools/wiki_extract.py`, `_chat_completion()` calls `src.tools._llm.generate_text(prompt, model=model)` and has no way to receive `model_config.provider`, `model_config.host`, or `model_config.parameters`. Any installation that points `eval_model` at a non-default endpoint, uses `openai-async://`, or relies on per-model parameters will now send wiki-maintainer traffic to the default tool client instead of the configured transport. That is a behavior regression in a supported configuration path, not a refactor-only change.
Suggestion: Preserve the full transport contract when delegating to `wiki_extract`. Either thread the full `ModelConfig` through `update_wiki_from_chapter()` and `_chat_completion()`, or make the tool accept provider/host/parameter overrides explicitly and pass them from `WikiMaintainerAgent.run()`.

#### Warning Findings

[W-01] Wiki maintainer documentation still describes prompt-loader and streamed-provider behavior that no longer exists
Category: Documentation
Severity: Warning
File: docs/features/story-orchestrator.md
Lines: 133-144
Description: The updated docs still state that Python-native agents stream output through `provider.stream_text(...)` and that the wiki maintainer lazily loads its prompt via `_get_system_prompt()`. Current code no longer does either: `WikiMaintainerAgent` imports `update_wiki_from_chapter()` directly, never loads `prompts/agents/wiki-maintainer.md`, and performs the work inside `asyncio.to_thread(...)`. The same stale claim appears again in `docs/features/wiki-maintainer.md:184`, which says orchestration reads `prompts/agents/wiki-maintainer.md` through `agent_prompt_loader.py`. These are now false statements about the runtime contract.
Suggestion: Update both docs to describe the actual implementation: the wiki maintainer delegates to `tools.wiki_extract.update_wiki_from_chapter()` on a worker thread, emits progress/result events, and no longer streams prompt tokens or loads a prompt file during execution.

[W-02] New tests codify the transport regression instead of guarding against it
Category: Testing
Severity: Warning
File: tests/unit/test_wiki_maintainer.py
Lines: 161-184
Description: The added unit coverage explicitly asserts that `provider.stream_text` must not be called and only checks that the extractor receives `model="my-model"`. That test shape locks in the exact regression from [C-01]: it would still pass if `eval_model` were configured with `openai-async://wiki@host?temperature=0`, even though the implementation would silently drop the provider, host, and parameters. There is no regression test covering custom host/provider propagation or any equivalent transport override path.
Suggestion: Replace or extend these tests so they validate the full `eval_model` contract. At minimum, add coverage proving that custom host/provider/parameter settings survive the handoff into the extraction path, or intentionally document and test a new reduced contract if that behavior change is intended.

### Overall Assessment

This branch is not ready for merge as written. The feature works for the default model client path, but it regresses supported `eval_model` configurations by bypassing the injected provider contract, and the accompanying docs and tests currently hide that break instead of catching it. Fixing the transport propagation and then aligning the docs/tests with the real behavior should be sufficient to make the change reviewable again.
